Officer's narrative
Driver 1 was operating a sedan northbound on a Houston city street and was making a left turn at an intersection
when the front of the vehicle was struck by a pickup truck, Driver 2, which was proceeding straight through the
intersection. Driver 1 reported pain in the lower back and said the force of the impact pushed the body against the
seat and steering wheel. A Passenger was seated in the front right position and was also present in the sedan at the
time of the collision, a fact confirmed by the investigating officer and by statements from both drivers. No independent
witnesses were located at the scene, so the acocunt rests on the parteis involved. Photographs taken at the secne
show damage to the front bumper, the driver-side headlamp, and the hood of the sedan, along with a crushed right
front fender on the pickup. Driver 1 is listed as the named insured on the policy covering the sedan. The officer found
no prior damage to the sedan in the vehicle records or in statements given. Because the photographs show damage
to several areas, it is not clear at this stage whether all of the visible damage resulted from this single impact. The
reported back complaint is consistent with the mechanics of a side impact of this kind.
